Colonic mucin O-glycan degradation by enzyme mixtures

glyhub_GPST000643_O_S11B.Rd

Porcine colonic mucin oligosaccharide profiles after treatment with a Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron enzyme mixture, with or without BT3868. The experiment tests how adding this GH20 enzyme changes the residual glycans and digestion products after combined removal of terminal residues and substituents. Supplementary Table S11B contains 60 features across nine observations.

Usage

glyhub_GPST000643_O_S11B

Format

A glyexp::GlycomicSE with 60 features and 9 observations. The abundance assay is in percentage of source total glycan AUC.

Source

GlycoPOST GPST000643. Supplementary Table S11B, sheet named Table 11B (media-12.xlsx). Study: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.03.26.714468. Repository: https://glycopost.glycosmos.org/entry/GPST000643.

Details

Three source-labelled samples are reported for each of a no-enzyme control, an eleven-enzyme mixture and the same mixture supplemented with BT3868. The base mixture contains BT0455, BT4243, BT1625, BT3173, BT1636, BT1624, BT1626, BT4241, BT1628, BT4681 and BT0438. This is the S11B mixture; it does not include the additional BT4394 used in the distinct S11C experiment.

Measurements are percentages of source total glycan AUC. O-derived features include remaining substrate glycans and released enzymatic products. Sample 1-3 labels are retained without assigning a biological replicate type or pairing the conditions.

Compositions are typed for all features and 27 putative structures are encoded. Ambiguous structural text remains available for the other features.

See also

glyhub_data_conventions for missing-value handling, annotations and access to original measurements and source coordinates.
